answer: The cheapest defence against cloned agents is making cloning expensive. Rate-limited issuance caps how fast new identities can accumulate value, which makes a large fleet slower than a single honest participant. Think of it as a mirror the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single jade of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a walnut of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
